core.metanarrative_position: Whole-Bible review: Creation, rebellion, promise, Jesus, church, and new creation.

claims.statement: God keeps His promises across the story, from Abraham and Israel to Jesus and the hope of new creation.
God rescues His people and gives them good instruction, while human leaders and communities still need God’s faithful rule.
Jesus stands at the centre of God’s promised rescue, and the church lives in hope while awaiting God’s final renewal.

core.interpretation_skill: Retell sequence; identify cause and effect; connect to the big story without forced symbolism

learning.foundation_objective: Students can locate the cycle theme within Creation, rebellion, promise, Jesus, church, and new creation.
learning.extension_objective: Support the big idea with evidence, label the reasoning used, and identify one faithful response without overstating the text.

preparation.passage_context: Cycle 2 synthesis/review drawing on selected approved passages.
text_observations: God keeps His promises across the story, from Abraham and Israel to Jesus and the hope of new creation.
God rescues His people and gives them good instruction, while human leaders and communities still need God’s faithful rule.
interpretation_notes: Label direct text, synthesis, inference, framework position, and prudential application accurately.
Do not let a review or local calendar purpose override the context of a selected passage.
theological_guardrails: Keep synthesis concrete and story-shaped. Do not pressure children toward baptism or turn promises into guarantees of comfort, wealth, health, or immediate rescue.

activities.title: Promise Story Map
steps: Read the designated passages and record direct observations.
Place each observation or claim into the resource categories.
Discuss which conclusions require synthesis or inference.
Write one careful application that follows from the evidence.
activities.learning_link: Makes the lesson’s interpretation skill visible and concrete.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Draw the same categories on blank paper or complete the exercise verbally.

activities.title: Observation, Interpretation, or Application?
steps: Read several statements connected to the lesson.
Classify each statement as observation, interpretation/synthesis, or application.
Return to the passage and justify each classification.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Use verbal responses instead of written cards.

closing.prayer_prompt: Thank God for what the passage reveals and ask for wisdom to respond faithfully.

family.title: God Keeps His Promises: Whole-Story Synthesis
family.parent_intro: Read the selected passages first, keep the discussion evidence-based, and leave room for questions.

flow.instructions: Connect this lesson to something already learned in Cycle 2.
Read selected portions of the Cycle 2 passages and name direct observations.
Restate the big idea in your own words: Students can locate the cycle theme within Creation, rebellion, promise, Jesus, church, and new creation.
Use the Promise Story Map verbally, on paper, or with the provided worksheet.
Name one careful response that follows from the evidence without claiming more than the text supports.

questions: What does the passage directly say?
What does it show about God, Jesus, people, or the biblical story?
What is one response we can practise this week?

interactive.title: Promise Story Map

family.weekly_action: Revisit one Cycle 2 passage and explain what it says, what it means, and one faithful response.
family.prayer: Thank God for what the passage reveals and ask for help to respond faithfully.
family.parent_note: Questions are welcome. Do not force disclosure, certainty, giving, public prayer, baptism, or another public religious decision.

accessibility.plain_language_rule: Define unfamiliar terms from the passage before using theological shorthand.
neurodiversity_supports: Offer verbal or written response options.
Allow students to pass on personal-sharing questions.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of trauma, family finances, grief, or private spiritual decisions.
Do not pressure a child or young person toward baptism or another public response.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Answer from the passage, acknowledge uncertainty where needed, and route personal or safety concerns to appropriate adults rather than attempting to solve them in class.
